title: technical-hire-sprint-interview-suite-and-remote-onboard-checklist
content:
Purpose:
- Single working doc for a compact hiring sprint (IC3-IC5 eng) + parallel remote-first onboarding checklist.
- Goal: reduce time-to-offer and time-to-prod for new engineers while keeping calibration across interviewers.

Scope:
- Applies to SWE (backend/infra/serving-runtime) and SRE hires.
- Non-exhaustive; hiring manager can opt-in to role-specific exercises.

Quick summary timeline (target):
- Week 0: Requisition approved, JD live, panel assembled
- Week 1: Screen + take-home (if used)
- Week 2: Onsite (virtual) loop + hiring manager debrief
- Week 3: Offer, reference checks, salary calibration
- Day 0-30: rapid onboarding + mentor pairing

Interview structure (recommended default):
- Phone/Video screen (30m, recruiter) - culture fit, compensation, resume highlights
- Technical screen (45m, IC peer) - system design / coding depending on level
- Take-home (optional for IC4+) - 72-hour window, limited scope, time-boxed
- Virtual onsite (4 x 45m blocks):
  - 1: System design (architecture + tradeoffs)
  - 2: Debugging / code review (readability, tests, safety checks)
  - 3: Deep dive on past project (ownership, metrics, tradeoffs)
  - 4: Behavioral / collaboration (cross-team, incident handling)
- Debrief (30m) - hiring manager + panel synthesize scores

Interviewer roles & expectations:
- Interviewer 1 (system design owner): focus on end-to-end reasoning, scaling, cost/latency tradeoffs (relevant to inference).
- Interviewer 2 (coding/debug): expect clear tests, edge case handling, simple algorithms.
- Interviewer 3 (domain peer): ask about model serving, GPU infra, quantization experience when relevant.
- Interviewer 4 (manager/behavioral): leadership, cross-team communication, incident postmortem experience.

Scorecard (quick rubric):
- Scale 1-5 across categories; passing requires >=3 average and no category <2.
  - Technical mastery (system/coding)
  - Product sense / tradeoffs (latency, cost)
  - Ownership & delivery (metrics, shipping)
  - Collaboration & communication
  - Learning agility (can pick up new infra)

Specific prompts (bank, use 1-2 per interview):
- System design: "Design an inference routing layer for multi-tenant workloads that minimizes tail latency while allowing model fallbacks." (probe: caching, KV cache, routing policy)
- Debugging/code: "Given this snippet that manipulates kv-cache keys, find the bug and add a unit test that catches it."
- Ownership deep dive: "Tell me about a time you shipped a perf improvement with measurable cost wins. How did you validate it?"
- Behavioral: "Describe a cross-team disagreement on rollback policy during an incident. How did you resolve it?"

Take-home guidelines (if used):
- Problem: 3–5 hour reasonable effort; provide skeleton repo; ask for explanation doc + tests.
- Scoring: correctness, clarity of README/assumptions, test coverage, deployment thought notes.
- Return window: 72 hours; allow 24h extension if requested (document reason).

Interviewer calibration notes (to share in prep):
- Use SRE/serving-runtime examples to anchor system questions.
- Penalize wild guesses; reward structured assumptions + tradeoff analysis.
- Document calibration examples in Confluence page (link in linked_artifacts).

Hiring manager checklist (pre-loop):
- [ ] Finalize JD + must-have vs nice-to-have list
- [ ] Panel slots booked (timezone-aware, >=2 interviewers from role team)
- [ ] Interview guides assigned to each interviewer
- [ ] Compensation band approved by People Ops
- [ ] Hiring rubric shared (this doc)

Candidate experience notes (recruiter):
- Send panel agenda + interviewer names 48h before loop
- Share expected prep: language/tooling, take-home instructions (if any)
- Offer timeline clarity: "We aim to decide within 48 hours of onsite"

Offer & reference checks:
- Soft-offer call script (template in Confluence)
- 2 references minimum (preferably managers + peer)
- Escalation: if conflicting references, escalate to hiring manager + head of eng for tie-break

Remote-first onboarding checklist (Day 0 -> Day 30):
- Pre-day0 (before start date):
  - [ ] IT assets order placed (laptop config, monitor, dongles) - owner: ops
  - [ ] Account requests queued (Slack, Google, GitHub, internal infra tenants) - owner: infra oncall
  - [ ] Manager welcome email + first-week agenda sent
  - [ ] Mentor assigned (shadow plan + weekly sync)
- Day 0:
  - [ ] Welcome call (30m) with manager: expectations, first projects
  - [ ] 1h team intro + system walkthrough (record)
  - [ ] Security & compliance checklist (KMS access request if needed)
  - [ ] Access to dev cluster + self-service runbook link
- Week 1:
  - [ ] Small onboarding ticket assigned: run a small end-to-end deploy in staging (paired with mentor)
  - [ ] Meet & greets: product, SRE, infra (15-30m each)
  - [ ] Engineering tools checklist completed (CI, tickets, code search, release train)
- Week 2-4:
  - [ ] First small PR merged (goal: infra or docs improvement)
  - [ ] 1:1 cadence set (weekly) + first 30-day goal alignment
  - [ ] Security and incident drills intro (shadow on-call rotation preparation)

Mentor pairing (practical):
- Mentor expectations: weekly 1:1 (30-45m), pair on first onboarding ticket, review PRs first 2 weeks, triage early questions asynchronously
- Mentor opt-in form: reproducible checklist for mentors (linked in artifacts)

Access & provisioning SLA (targets):
- Laptop delivered by Day -1 if possible
- Primary accounts provisioned Day 0 (target 95%)
- Elevated infra access (test cluster): within 7 business days (request flow documented)

Success metrics (to track for continuous improvement):
- Time-to-offer (target <= 21 days from first screen)
- Offer acceptance rate (target >= 70%)
- Time-to-first-merge (target <= 21 days)
- New hire 30-day health score (manager survey) >= 4/5

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we centralize take-homes in a shared repo for consistency? (pros/cons)
- Decide explicit policy for 'no take-home' vs 'take-home required' by level
- Create short interviewer training video (5–7m) demonstrating good vs bad debriefs

Action items (owners):
- Maya T: draft recruiter email templates + add to linked_artifacts (due 2026-02-10)
- Ibrahim K: create shared take-home repo skeleton (due 2026-02-17)
- Janelle P: draft mentor opt-in checklist and distribute to infra team (due 2026-02-24)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep interview loops to <=4 interviews to lower fatigue
- Encourage async debriefs when possible (fill scorecard first)
- Track timezone preference early for distributed candidates

References:
- See CONFLUENCE-1234 for company-wide calibration notes
- JIRA-HIRE-789 contains a recent hiring sprint retrospective with lessons learned

End of working draft.
